newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Britain appoints new ambassador to Beijing.
newsitem.headline: Britain appoints new ambassador to Beijing.

text.p: Britain has appointed Tony Galsworthy as ambassador to China, it announced in Hong Kong.
He will take up his appointment in December to replace retiring Leonard Appleyard, the British Trade Commission in Hong Kong said in a statement late on Monday.

Galsworthy, now in the U.K. Cabinet Office, was a senior British representative in a Sino-British diplomatic body that worked on the details of Hong Kong's transition to Chinese rule. "The Queen has been pleased to approve the appointment of Mr Tony Galsworthy CMG to be Her Majesty's Ambassador to the People's Republic of China in succession to Sir Leonard Appleyard KCMG," the statement said.

China will regain sovereignty over Hong Kong on July 1, ending 156 years of British colonial rule. Beijing ceded the territory to London when it was defeated in the Opium Wars in the mid-19th century.
